source.title: The role of the anterior prefrontal cortex in human cognition

confidence_rationale: Canonical (pre-2015 but foundational) demonstration that holding a main goal in a pending state WHILE executing subgoals recruits a dissociable substrate -- the precise functional operation ARC-105's what_would_answer specifies. Confidence is capped by 1999-era fMRI methods, small-sample subtraction logic, and the two decades of contested reinterpretation of frontopolar function that followed.
failure_signatures: Neither working memory alone nor dual-task attention-switching alone elicited the frontopolar response, so abstract-goal maintenance is not reducible to holding more items or to switching faster -- an architecture that models it as either will not reproduce the dissociation.
The pending main goal must survive the subgoal episode; a representation overwritten by the currently executing subgoal is exactly the failure ARC-105 predicts for a single-level encoding.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Bilateral frontopolar prefrontal cortex is selectively activated when subjects must keep a main goal in mind while performing concurrent subgoals; this activation appeared neither for working-memory load alone nor for dual-task sequential attention allocation, leading the authors to conclude that frontopolar cortex selectively mediates holding goals in mind while exploring and processing secondary goals.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the operational form of ARC-105's test condition: superordinate-goal maintenance ACROSS concrete-subgoal execution is a distinct function with a distinct substrate, separable from both memory capacity and task switching. It supports the claim's premise that the abstract goal must be encoded somewhere the executing subgoal does not overwrite -- i.e. at a distinct level -- rather than competing for the same single-scale representation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Selective ACTIVATION is not evidence that the two goals are encoded at distinct GRANULARITY levels; a dissociable region could equally hold a same-format goal in a protected buffer, which is a different architecture (separate store) from the one ARC-105 asserts (distinct granularity level). The study is also 1999 fMRI with subtraction-based inference, and frontopolar function has been repeatedly recontextualised since -- including by Badre & Nee 2018, filed alongside, which displaces the hierarchy apex away from rostrolateral PFC. Treat as strong evidence for the FUNCTION being dissociable, weak evidence for the specific REPRESENTATIONAL format.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults; blocked fMRI with branching, working-memory and dual-task control conditions.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality reflects foundational status offset by 1999 methods and small samples. Mapping fidelity held at 0.7 by the store-versus-level ambiguity, which is the single biggest interpretive gap between this paper and ARC-105's actual commitment.
